module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Single-clock FPGA top shell that owns the 128-bit transport endpoints, compact register window, local safety enforcement, and bounded scalar actuator drive-out. The top module is the RTL ownership point for packet sequencing, validation, fallback selection, and status accumulation; it does not implement surrogate inference.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Use a simple request/response transport controller plus a separate safety/command acceptance path. Outbound requests are issued only when enabled and when the outbound channel can accept a packet. Inbound responses are accepted only when valid, not duplicate, not out-of-order, and not stale. A small set of configuration registers governs enable, safe command, clamp limits, rate limiting, timeout, and stale thresholds. The control plane updates atomically per register address access.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain compact sequential state for request sequencing, last accepted sequence, last accepted actuator command, age/watchdog tracking, and latched fault/status flags. Use a minimal fallback state progression consistent with the described states IDLE, ARMED, ACTIVE, TIMEOUT_FALLBACK, and FAULT_HOLD, with deterministic transition behavior driven by enable, response validity, timeout, and fault conditions. Any optional history or telemetry storage should be treated as FPGA BRAM-backed storage via the provided memory contract, not as flattened registers.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive cmd_out_valid/cmd_out_data as outbound request packets and consume cmd_out_ready as backpressure. Consume cmd_in_valid/cmd_in_data as inbound response packets and drive cmd_in_ready according to acceptance capacity. Drive actuator_cmd and actuator_cmd_valid only from locally validated and bounded recommendations or from the configured safe fallback command when required. Drive status_flags from latched event and fault indicators, and return cfg_rdata from the register window with current configuration and status readback.
ownership_notes: Top-level port ownership remains with adaptive_aero_control_top.
No hierarchy renaming or port renaming is introduced.
The top module is the required synthesizable design top, not a status-only, telemetry-only, register-bank-only, or leaf module.
The RTL contract forwards compact packets to an external reference service and enforces local safety before actuator drive-out.
No surrogate model constants or assumed aerodynamic outputs are encoded in RTL.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_transport
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Compact packet transport and validation block that formats outbound 128-bit request packets, depacketizes inbound 128-bit response packets, and performs sequence/age checks with minimal control logic. It is descriptive transport logic only and does not infer or emulate the external model.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Track a monotonically increasing request sequence counter and last accepted response sequence. Generate request-issued and response-received pulses for downstream status accumulation. Reject responses that are duplicate, out-of-order, stale, or otherwise invalid before they can influence actuator acceptance. Honor valid/ready backpressure in both stream directions.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Hold only the small sequencing and comparison state required for request generation, response validation, and age comparison. Any packet metadata fields are internal to the 128-bit format and remain compact, carrying only what is needed for sequence, age/timestamp, flags, handle/descriptor context, and candidate command metadata.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Provide compact depacketized command candidate and metadata to the safety pipeline while also producing outbound request packets from configuration state and the request sequence counter. Emit status indications for request issuance and response reception without exposing any model internals.
ownership_notes: Owns transport-side packet interpretation only; actuator authority remains with the safety block.
Sequence tracking is monotonic for requests, and response comparison is used to reject duplicates and out-of-order packets.
Any optional history or telemetry storage must be mapped through the FPGA BRAM wrapper rather than flattened into registers.
The transport layer only forwards compact requests and compact responses; it does not implement inference.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_safety
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Deterministic safety and command-bounding block that consumes validated command candidates and converts them into bounded scalar actuator drive-out with clamp, optional rate limit, timeout handling, and fallback selection.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Apply programmable minimum and maximum clamp limits first, then optionally apply step-rate limiting versus the previously accepted command. If the command is stale, timed out, duplicate, out-of-order, invalid, or if the design is disabled or faulted, select the configured safe fallback command. Use a simple fallback progression consistent with IDLE, ARMED, ACTIVE, TIMEOUT_FALLBACK, and FAULT_HOLD without introducing unnecessary complexity.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain the previously accepted command, latch fault/event conditions, and retain counters for timeout/stale/clamp/fallback events. On reset, force actuator_cmd_valid low and place the output in the configured safe fallback state or a conservative default. The state strategy is deterministic and single-clock, with no dependence on external surrogate timing.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive actuator_cmd as a bounded 16-bit scalar command and assert actuator_cmd_valid only when a validated command has passed safety checks. Provide compact status_flags plus fault and debug counters for firmware visibility and register readback. The output path must remain deterministic under timeout, stale-data rejection, duplicate/out-of-order rejection, or external service unavailability.
ownership_notes: Safety policy is locally enforced and does not depend on external surrogate behavior.
Timeout, stale, duplicate, and out-of-order conditions lead to deterministic fallback or rejection as required by the contract.
Status reporting includes whether a request was issued, a response was received, a clamp occurred, a timeout occurred, or fallback was engaged.
The block drives only compact scalar actuator outputs; no tensor, mesh, or large payload port is exposed.

module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_registers
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Compact control-plane register window with 8-bit address and 32-bit data access, intended for atomic configuration updates and status/counter readback.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Decode the specified register map for enable, safe fallback command, clamp limits, rate-limit enable and step, timeout threshold, stale threshold, status flags, fault counters, and debug counters. Writes update the targeted register atomically per access. Reads return current configuration and latched status values.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Store only the small set of configuration and readback-visible status values defined by the register contract. Latched fault/status information is preserved for firmware logging. The register interface remains compact and does not expand into a large register bank hierarchy.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Return cfg_rdata with the selected register contents and expose configuration outputs to the rest of the top-level shell. Feed status_flags_in, fault_counters_in, and debug_counters_in into the readback path so firmware sees the latest latched events and counters.
ownership_notes: Uses cfg_addr, cfg_wdata, cfg_rdata, cfg_we, and cfg_re exactly as defined in the hierarchy.
Accepts status and counter inputs from downstream logic for readback packaging.
Register storage is control-plane state only and does not redefine design hierarchy.
Reads and writes remain limited to the specified compact window and do not expose surrogate internals.

fsm_intent: A minimal fallback FSM is implied by the spec and should remain simple. The intent is to support deterministic behavior with states such as IDLE, ARMED, ACTIVE, TIMEOUT_FALLBACK, and FAULT_HOLD, driven by enable, accepted response validity, timeout/stale conditions, and latched fault conditions. No additional complex control machine is implied beyond this bounded safety progression.
datapath_intent: Request-side datapath: pack compact 128-bit outbound request packets from configuration state, request sequence counter, and the latest relevant control context.
Response-side datapath: unpack 128-bit inbound response packets into candidate actuator command, sequence, age, validity, and error metadata.
Safety datapath: compare candidate command against min/max limits, optionally apply rate limiting relative to the previously accepted command, and select fallback when required.

Storage intent: keep only compact sequential state in registers; if any optional history/telemetry storage is needed, implement it through the technology-neutral FPGA BRAM wrapper u_history_bram rather than flip-flops.

Output mapping: cmd_out_valid/cmd_out_data are driven by outbound request generation, cmd_in_ready reflects response acceptance capacity, actuator_cmd/actuator_cmd_valid reflect the bounded accepted command or safe fallback, and status_flags reflects latched event/fault conditions.
sequencing_notes: Maintain a monotonically increasing request sequence counter.
Store the last accepted sequence and compare inbound response sequence values to reject duplicates and out-of-order packets.
Track response age or timestamp against the configured stale threshold and watchdog timeout threshold.
Treat stale, duplicate, out-of-order, malformed, or timed-out responses as non-acceptable for actuator drive-out.
All register writes are to be treated atomically per address access.
Backpressure on both valid/ready streams must be honored without assuming external service timing.
timing_notes: All sequential logic is clocked by clk and reset by rst_n.
Reset is active-low and synchronously deasserted in the RTL contract.
Combinational next-state logic should determine stream handshake decisions, packet acceptance, safety decisions, and output valid behavior.
The design must remain single-clock, deterministic, FPGA-synthesizable, and free of unsized arithmetic or unsynthesizable system tasks.
Top-level scalar-equivalent I/O count remains below the stated limit and only compact scalar actuator outputs are exposed.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
